## §3 — Process learnings (the arc)

This section is the spine; the §4 gap table cross-references it.

### 3.1 — The wrong-PASS (KC-02): the close-gate asserted the wrong invariant
The KC-02 close-gate rendered the transcript and read it (satisfying the *letter* of `[[feedback_render_transcript_close_gate]]` Rules 1–2), yet still read PASS over wrong behavior — because what it *asserted* was **no-400 / no-orphan / facts-present**, all of which were genuinely true, while the **disposition** (does the post-target tail actually shrink?) was never asserted. P0-KC-03 F-9 nails the mechanism: KC-02's clause-(iii) re-append makes the cluster internally PAIRED, so `enforce_call_atomic_backstop` sees no orphan (`dangling=false orphan=false`) on the *leaky* render — the no-400 invariant is structurally incapable of catching a keep-whole-when-it-should-shrink defect. **"Wire rendered + read + no-400" is necessary but NOT sufficient; the gate must assert the DISPOSITION against the intended contract.** This is the central lesson of the arc and the KC-02 root cause. → §5 proposal #1.

### 3.2 — Design-drift from the user's model (KC-02): a USER-DIVERGENT lock that drifted from #77 intent
The (B) "keep-whole" heuristic was a USER-DIVERGENT F1 lock (iter-1 recommended (a) reclaim-to-breadcrumb). It drifted from the user's *original* #77 t-tag / surgical-removal intent: the simple contract (shrink-tail + surgical atomicity) was right all along — KC-01's own close-gate §4 had even leaned toward option (a) "reclaim the abandoned tail." The drift was not caught at plan time because no artifact framed the candidate dispositions *against the user's stated revert model*; the fork was locked on internal-mechanism grounds. **A USER-DIVERGENT lock on a model-semantics fork deserves an explicit "does this match the user's stated contract?" check before it becomes the spec the auditors verify against.** → §5 proposal #1 (Rule 4) + #6 (audit-baseline note).

### 3.3 — Why three auditors all PASSed a wrong disposition
KC-02 ran a Large 3-auditor envelope and all three PASSed (A 8/8, B 8/8, C 6/6). They were **not wrong about what they checked** — they verified the implementation matched the *plan's* (B) disposition, the tests matched the plan, the docs matched the code, no-400 held. The defect is upstream of the audit: **the auditors verify code ↔ plan ↔ tests internal consistency, NOT the plan's disposition against the user's contract.** When the spec itself is the misread, a green audit sweep cannot catch it. This is structural, not an auditor failure — and it is precisely why the *disposition-asserting close-gate* (a check OUTSIDE the code↔plan↔test triangle, against the user's actual model) is the load-bearing gate for model-facing semantics. → §4 gap row 2; §5 proposals #1, #2.

### 3.4 — Investigation-first payoff (KC-03): refuted a hypothesis + caught a plan undercount
Covered in §2; the process point: for an **S2 core-tool correctness chunk that supersedes a prior ADR and carries a "more fundamental change" uncertainty**, `investigation=true` was decisive — it converted two unknowns (fix-locus depth; carry-forward test set) into reproduced facts before a line of production code was written. This is the profile where P0 should be the default, not opt-in. → §5 proposal #3.

### 3.5 — Plan carry-forward-test-inversion undercount (KC-03)
The plan named 3 inversions; 5 were needed. Root cause: the planner's grep keyed on the obviously-named `row_*`/`matrix_*` tests and missed 3 `edge_*` tests (`edge_post_cluster_followon_dropped`, `edge_mixed_on_off_trunk`, `edge_two_cluster_isolation`) that assert the *same* superseded clause-(iii) keep-whole predicate under different names. **When a chunk inverts/removes a prior-cycle disposition, the completeness condition is "grep ALL tests asserting the superseded predicate," not "grep the obviously-named ones."** Caught at P0 only because investigation-first re-grounded the test set; a non-investigation cycle would have shipped a 3-of-5 inversion and surfaced the other 2 as audit FAILs or, worse, as stale-green tests. → §5 proposal #4.

### 3.6 — Educate+enforce for model-facing format expectations (`[nN]`-echo follow-up)
The model echoed its own `[nN]` node markers into content. Two-layer fix: **educate** (tool-doc note: "don't write your own `[nN]` tags," commit `0451575`) dampens but does not guarantee (measured partial 2→1); **enforce** (deterministic render-pass strip of a model-echoed leading `[nN]` before prepending the real marker, commit `1c5e168`) guarantees. The discipline learned: a model-facing doc note is a probabilistic nudge — pair it with deterministic enforcement, AND **measure the doc-note effect empirically before adding the kernel fix** (so the kernel fix is justified by data, not assumed). → §5 proposal #5.

### 3.7 — ADR-supersession chain hygiene (ADR-0001 → 0002 → 0003)
Three cycles produced a clean supersession chain: ADR-0001 (call-atomicity) → ADR-0002 §D2.1 (the (B) misread) → ADR-0003 (the corrected contract, SUPERSEDES ADR-0002 §D2.1). Each superseded ADR carries an inline supersession note + a bumped verified-header; ADR-0003 cross-refs the chain. This worked, and the discipline is worth naming as a reusable pattern (a wrong-but-shipped ADR is *superseded-in-part inline*, never deleted — the audit trail of *why we changed our mind* is itself valuable). → §6 open-follow-up note.

## §5 — Standards updates proposed

> Each row cites a specific target + concrete versioned change + gap citation. Standards updates surface as PROPOSALS — orchestrator + user apply them separately. §3.5 audit-driven updates appear here (cross-referenced, not double-counted).

### Proposal #1 — Close-gate asserts the DISPOSITION (refine `[[feedback_render_transcript_close_gate]]`) — **HIGH** (the KC-02 wrong-PASS root cause)

**Target:** `/root/.claude/projects/-root-projects-phi/memory/feedback_render_transcript_close_gate.md` (multi-rule memory; already carries Rules 1–3 → add **Rule 4** per the `Rule N` memory convention).

**Concrete change — add Rule 4 to the "How to apply" list:**

> - **Rule 4 (disposition-assert)**: For a model-facing change with an *intended behavioral contract* (a revert disposition, a denial semantic, a context-shape invariant), rendering + reading the transcript is necessary but NOT sufficient — the close-gate MUST **assert each rule of the intended contract against the rendered wire**, not merely that the request is well-formed (no-400 / no-orphan / no-crash / "facts present"). A wire can be perfectly balanced (no-400) AND carry the *wrong disposition*. Enumerate the contract's rules up front, then assert each one shows the intended behavior in the model's exact input. If you can only assert "no error / well-formed," you have NOT validated the fix — you have validated that a wrong behavior is well-formed.

**Rationale / origin:** KC-02 `d835a363` shipped a close-gate that rendered + read the wire (Rules 1–3 satisfied) and asserted no-400 / no-orphan / facts-present — all true — yet PASSed over a wrong disposition (the tail was kept, not shrunk). P0-KC-03 F-9 proves no-400 is *structurally blind* to a keep-whole-when-shrink-expected defect. The user caught it by reading the turn-3 request and asking "does the tail actually shrink?" — the disposition question Rule 4 makes mandatory. KC-03's disposition-asserting close-gate (R1/R3/R2a/R2 each asserted on both drivers) is the corrected exemplar to cite in the memory's "Why."

### Proposal #2 — Promote the phi-core kernel close-gate harness to a reusable template/skill — **MEDIUM**

**Target:** new `/root/projects/phi/.claude/skills/phi-core-close-gate/SKILL.md` (analogous to the i-phi HTC harness); cross-reference from `phi-core/CLAUDE.md` "Build & Development" and the KC-01 retro-context "reusable pattern" note.

**Concrete change:** codify the validated pattern as a skill:

2. Parameterized runner `IPHI_MODEL_OVERRIDE=<driver> bash run-harness-htc.sh` over the strongest-available open-source drivers (per `[[feedback_htc_cohort_strongest_open_source]]`).
3. A reusable disposition-reader **shipped as a script** (`assert-disposition.py <wire-request.json> <contract-rules>`) that reads `turn-N.request.json` and asserts each contract rule — NOT inline `python3 -c` (closes the §3.5 inline-heredoc prompt cluster, §5 #8).
4. The secret/events-`.gitignore` pattern + cycle folder layout under `i-phi/docs/e2e-test/cycles/kc<NN>-close-gate-<hex>/`.

**Rationale:** the runner + fixture composed cleanly across KC-02→KC-03 (5 live cells, two drivers) and is the kernel lane's only end-to-end acceptance surface (phi-core has no daemon of its own). KC-01 retro-context flagged this as "standards candidate #2"; three cycles of hand-rolling now justify the promotion. Pairs with Proposal #1 (the skill bakes in the disposition-assert as the close-gate's authoritative signal).

### Proposal #3 — `investigation=true` default for kernel-correctness chunks — **MEDIUM-HIGH**

**Target:** `/root/projects/phi/.claude/agents/chunk-initiate*` (Phase 0.5 investigation-gate) + a one-line note in `/root/projects/phi/CLAUDE.md` "Agents" → `chunk-p0-investigator` description.

**Concrete change:** make `investigation=true` the **default** (not opt-in) when ANY of:
- the chunk is **S2+ core-tool / kernel-render correctness** (revert/braking/context-shape semantics), OR
- the chunk **supersedes a prior ADR** (the spec is being changed, not extended), OR
- the chunk carries a **"more fundamental change" / fix-locus-depth uncertainty** in its forward-scope risk section.

Default stays opt-in (off) for additive feature chunks with no correctness uncertainty.

**Rationale:** KC-03's P0 refuted a wrong hypothesis (F-2/F-3: trunk walk already shrinks) AND caught the plan undercount (3→5 inversions) — both before code, zero downstream rework. KC-02, by contrast, locked a disposition without a contract-grounded investigation and shipped a misread. The three triggers above are exactly the KC-03 profile; making P0 the default there converts the KC-02 class of miss into a pre-plan reproduced fact.

### Proposal #4 — Plan carry-forward-test-inversion completeness check — **MEDIUM**

**Target:** `/root/projects/phi/.claude/agents/chunk-planner.md` (a §6/§7 carry-forward check) + `/root/projects/phi/CLAUDE.md` orchestrator gate-1.5 pre-archival checks (a P-orch addition).

**Concrete change:** add a check: *when a chunk inverts or removes a prior-cycle disposition, enumerate the inversion set by the SUPERSEDED PREDICATE, not by test-name shape.* Concretely — grep for the assertion the superseded disposition encodes (e.g. the keep-whole `trunk_has_tool_result("pcall_b")` / re-append assertions), across ALL test names (`row_*`, `matrix_*`, **and** `edge_*` and any others) plus **test-module narrative comments**, and list every match as an inversion candidate. The plan's inversion count must equal the predicate-grep count or explain each exclusion.

**Rationale:** the KC-03 planner named 3 of 5 inversions because the grep keyed on obvious names and missed 3 `edge_*` tests asserting the same predicate (cycle-audit §6 D-1); the stale test-module comment (D-3) is the same class. Predicate-anchored grep closes both. Caught at P0 this cycle only because investigation-first re-grounded the set — Proposal #3 + #4 are complementary belts.

### Proposal #5 — Educate+enforce pattern for model-facing format expectations — **LOW-MEDIUM**

**Target:** a new short user-memory `[[feedback_educate_then_enforce]]` under `/root/.claude/projects/-root-projects-phi/memory/` (multi-rule, `Rule N` form).

**Concrete change — capture the two-layer pattern:**
> When the model is expected to *not* do something formatting-wise (echo its own `[nN]` tags, emit a forbidden token, mis-order a field): **Rule 1 (educate)** — add a tool-doc / system-prompt note nudging the behavior; this DAMPENS but does not GUARANTEE (it is probabilistic). **Rule 2 (measure)** — render a representative transcript and measure the doc-note's empirical effect (e.g. echo count 2→1) BEFORE adding a kernel fix, so the deterministic fix is justified by data, not assumed. **Rule 3 (enforce)** — pair the doc note with a deterministic kernel/render-pass guarantee (e.g. strip a model-echoed leading `[nN]` before prepending the real marker) for the cases education doesn't cover.

**Rationale:** the post-KC-03 `[nN]`-echo follow-up did exactly this in the right order — educate (`0451575`), measured partial 2→1, then enforce (`1c5e168`). Naming the pattern makes it reusable for the next model-facing format expectation (and prevents the anti-pattern of jumping straight to a kernel fix without measuring whether education sufficed).

### Proposal #6 — "Disposition-vs-user-contract" baseline at plan-lock for model-semantics forks — **MEDIUM**

**Target:** `/root/projects/phi/.claude/agents/chunk-planner.md` (fork-presentation for model-semantics forks) + `[[feedback_locked_fork_details_appendix]]` (the locked-fork appendix already required before approval).

**Concrete change:** when a fork chooses a **model-facing behavioral disposition** (a revert disposition, denial semantic, context-shape choice), the locked-fork appendix MUST carry a one-line **"matches user's stated contract?"** anchor for the chosen option — citing the user's stated model (issue text / prior chunk intent) the disposition is checked against. A USER-DIVERGENT lock on such a fork additionally requires an explicit "this diverges from option (a)/the prior intent because <user rationale>" note, so the divergence is recorded as a *deliberate contract choice*, not an internal-mechanism preference.

**Rationale:** KC-02's (B) lock was USER-DIVERGENT and drifted from the #77 surgical-removal intent (§3.2); no artifact framed (B) against the user's stated revert model, so the misread became the spec the auditors verified (gap row 2). This anchor surfaces the contract-match question at lock time — the cheapest place to catch a disposition drift. Complements Proposal #1 (close-gate catches it end-to-end; this catches it at plan-lock).

### Proposal #7 — Add `RUSTFLAGS="" cargo test *` allow rule — **LOW** (from §3.5 §B(1))

**Target:** `/root/projects/phi/.claude/settings.json` `permissions.allow`.

**Concrete change:** add `Bash(RUSTFLAGS="" /root/rust-env/cargo/bin/cargo test *)`.

**Rationale:** 16 PermissionRequests this window for the empty-RUSTFLAGS cargo-test form (P0 `*_THROWAWAY` repro runs). settings.json has `cargo test *`, `RUSTFLAGS="-Dwarnings" cargo clippy *` and `... build *`, but no `RUSTFLAGS="" cargo test *` — the prefix blocks the bare-`cargo test` match. **Empirical-validation caveat** (per permissions-audit §B matcher-semantics discipline): before committing, run one representative `RUSTFLAGS="" /root/rust-env/cargo/bin/cargo test ... 2>&1 | tail -N` against a test settings.json carrying the candidate to confirm the `*` glob spans the `2>&1 | tail` trailing combo (the known space-form-glob quirk) — if it doesn't, prefer a literal form or drop the trailing pipe.

### Proposal #8 — Close-gate wire-reading: write-to-file scripts, not inline `python3 -c` heredocs — **LOW** (from §3.5 §B(2))

**Target:** the phi-core close-gate template/skill (Proposal #2) + a one-line reminder in `phi-core/CLAUDE.md` referencing the granular-bash-discipline.

**Concrete change:** the disposition-reader is shipped as `assert-disposition.py` (or `.sh`) and invoked as `python3 /abs/path/assert-disposition.py <args>` / `bash /abs/path/...` — one prompt per run — instead of inline multi-line `python3 -c "..."` heredocs that fragment into per-line PermissionRequests.

**Rationale:** the dominant prompt source this window (~70+ of 102) was newline-split fragments of inline Python transcript-readers. This is the documented granular-bash-discipline empirical quirk (multi-line bash/heredoc fragments split into per-line prompts). Writing the reader to a file collapses it to a single matched invocation. Folds into Proposal #2's harness (the reader becomes part of the reusable template).
